introduction_markdown: Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section 1 is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section 2 in 1 1/2 hours; you are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section 2 answer EITHER the a, b and c OR the d, e and f of each question. For your guidance the approximate mark(s) for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Non-programmable calculators are allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown: State the principle of moments. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: The **principle of moments** states that, for a body in equilibrium, the **sum of the clockwise moments about any point is equal to the sum of the anticlockwise moments about the same point**.

questions.enonce_markdown: State two conditions necessary for a system to be in equilibrium. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
For a system (a body) to be in equilibrium:

1. The **resultant force** acting on it must be **zero** (the forces in opposite directions balance: total upward force = total downward force, and so on).
2. The **resultant moment (turning effect) about any point must be zero**: the sum of the clockwise moments equals the sum of the anticlockwise moments about that point.

questions.enonce_markdown: The perpendicular distance from the handle of a door shutter to the hinges is $0.9\,\mathrm{m}$. Calculate the moment produced when the door handle is pulled with a force of $80\,\mathrm{N}$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The moment of a force about a point is the force multiplied by the **perpendicular distance** from the point to the line of action of the force:

$$\text{moment} = F\times d = 80\,\mathrm{N}\times 0.9\,\mathrm{m} = 72\,\mathrm{N\,m}$$

The moment produced about the hinges is **$72\,\mathrm{N\,m}$**.
